title: In-Network Machine Learning Using Programmable Network Devices: A Survey
domain: In-network machine learning with programmable data planes

analysis_policy.exclude_scope: References, author bios/photos, acknowledgments, appendix, nomenclature
analysis_policy.notes: Span tags retained; tables include mixed formatting.

section_flow.objective: Motivate in-network ML, review related work, state contributions/organization, and position ML-for-networking background.
key_components: Need for in-network ML with programmable devices
notable_moves: Keeps a short ML-for-networking primer within introduction to set context

evidence_locators.claim: States survey gap, contributions, organization, and provides ML-for-networking context.

section_flow.objective: Describe programmable data plane components (PISA, languages, targets, control plane) and in-network computing basics.
notable_moves: Pairs architecture/language/targets with control-plane discussion to frame feasibility

evidence_locators.claim: Explains PISA, data plane languages, targets, control plane, and in-network computing.

raw_headings: V. DEVELOPMENT TIMELINE OF IN-NETWORK MACHINE LEARNING
section_flow.objective: Classify in-network ML developments by model family, deployment scenarios, and limitations.
notable_moves: Timeline followed by per-model-family taxonomy plus deployment scenarios and limitations

evidence_locators.claim: Provides in-network ML timeline and classifies models (tree-based, BNN, RL, others) with deployment scenarios and limitations.

locator.heading: V. DEVELOPMENT TIMELINE OF IN-NETWORK MACHINE LEARNING

raw_headings: VI. IMPLEMENTATION OF IN-NETWORK MACHINE LEARNING ALGORITHMS
section_flow.objective: Survey implementations of in-network ML across learning paradigms.
notable_moves: Large implementation section broken down by learning paradigm with extensive tables

evidence_locators.claim: Details implementations of supervised, unsupervised, semi-supervised, and RL in-network ML.

locator.heading: VI. IMPLEMENTATION OF IN-NETWORK MACHINE LEARNING ALGORITHMS

section_flow.objective: Enumerate challenges/limitations of in-network ML and discuss solutions.
notable_moves: Challenges framed with solutions per constraint (stages, memory, data types, computation)

evidence_locators.claim: Lists challenges and solutions including stages, memory, data types, computation, and other limits.

raw_headings: VIII. LESSONS LEARNED AND FUTURE TRENDS
section_flow.objective: Summarize lessons learned and outline future trends for in-network ML.
notable_moves: Lessons and future trends are short and paired

evidence_locators.claim: Provides lessons learned and outlines future trends.

locator.heading: VIII. LESSONS LEARNED AND FUTURE TRENDS

section_flow.objective: Conclude the survey and restate outlook.

hook.evidence: Highlights need for in-network ML using programmable data planes to meet performance demands.

gap.evidence: Notes limited surveys combining programmable data planes with in-network ML implementations and challenges.

yes_but.evidence: Acknowledges prior ML-for-networking works but stresses missing programmable data-plane focus.

contribution.evidence: Lists contributions across data-plane background, in-network ML taxonomy, implementations, and challenges.

organization.evidence: Provides organization of sections in introduction.

scope_boundary.evidence: Scope limited to in-network ML using programmable network devices covering models, implementations, and challenges.

rhetorical_moves_global.reader_contract_pattern: Motivate in-network ML; provide data-plane basics; timeline and model taxonomy; detail implementations; list challenges/solutions; summarize lessons/trends; conclude.

taxonomy.classification_strategy: by model family and deployment scenario

visuals_tables.layout_logic: Multiple tables summarize data-plane components and in-network ML implementations; figures illustrate architectures and timelines; challenges/lessons text-heavy.

figures.purpose: show programmable data-plane components and in-network ML flow

tables.purpose: summarize programmable data-plane elements or in-network ML implementations

lesson_blocks.lesson: Architecture/language/target constraints shape feasible in-network ML designs.
Tree/BNN/RL/other models map differently onto hardware constraints and timelines.
Supervised/unsupervised/semi-supervised/RL implementations trade accuracy for latency/resource budgets.
Stage, memory, data type, and compute limits dominate deployment barriers; solutions often co-design models with hardware.

synthesis.aha_moment: Aligning model families and implementations with data-plane constraints, then tackling stage/memory/data/compute limits, turns in-network ML from ad hoc deployments into a structured design space.

style.section_openers_pattern: Introduce component/domain then enumerate subtopics with tables/figures; frequent use of lists.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Intro + data-plane primer
steps: Motivate in-network ML and note survey gap.
Introduce programmable data plane components (PISA, languages, targets, control plane) before model taxonomy.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Gives readers the hardware context needed to understand later model/implementation choices.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Timeline + model-family taxonomy
steps: Provide a development timeline of in-network ML.
Classify models by family (tree, BNN, RL, other) with deployment scenarios and limitations.
Use tables to keep comparisons clear.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Chronology plus taxonomy clarifies maturity and gaps across model types.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Implementation by learning paradigm
steps: Group implementations into supervised, unsupervised, semi-supervised, and RL.
Anchor with tables summarizing key designs.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Parallel structure simplifies comparison across learning paradigms under hardware limits.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Challenge-to-solution pairing
steps: List constraints (stages, memory, data types, computation, other).
Pair each with representative solution strategies.
Keep concise to feed into lessons/future trends.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Direct pairing makes the research agenda actionable.

notes: Counts heuristic; heavy lists and equations; many tables summarizing data-plane components and in-network ML implementations. Abbreviation-like tables present.
